common.scope: The catalogue concerns indecomposable data with identity symmetrizer and diagonal leading matrix. Rank counts species; it need not equal the number of vertices of the reconstructed quiver.
common.definition:
Choose positive integer delays r₁, …, rₙ and polynomial matrices N₊, N₋ with nonnegative integer coefficients. In row i, every exponent p obeys 0 < p < rᵢ. Opposite signs have disjoint support in each entry.

N₀(z) = diag(1 + zr₁, …, 1 + zrₙ),   A±(z) = N₀(z) − N±(z)
A₊(z) A₋(z−1)T = A₋(z) A₊(z−1)T

Indecomposability means that no simultaneous index permutation splits both matrices into two nonempty diagonal blocks. Finite type means periodicity of the associated universal Y-system.
common.theorem: Every finite-type datum in this scope is an admissible rational time rescaling and species shift of exactly one displayed representative, up to simultaneous index permutation and sign exchange. Conversely every such admissible transform is of finite type.
common.status: The rank-three through rank-six proofs combine mathematical reductions, exact arithmetic, exhaustive enumeration and solver UNSAT answers. These are computer-assisted classifications. The reader summarizes the arguments and links the complete sources; viewing a record does not rerun the classification.

references.title: Mizuno: rank-two classification (arXiv:2301.13239)
references.use: Definitions; simultaneous positivity, Lemma 3.3; periodicity from two-sided reddening, Proposition 2.7; changes of slices, §3.1.

references.title: Mizuno: T-data (arXiv:1912.05710)
references.use: The general T-datum framework and arbitrary-rank simultaneous positivity, Theorem 5.5.

3.decomposable: Decomposable rank-three data are direct sums of components with rank partitions 2 + 1 or 1 + 1 + 1. Component time scales can be chosen independently.

steps.title: 1. Bound the constant coefficient sums
steps.html:
Write P = N₊(1) and M = N₋(1). Finite type implies a common positive row vector v with v(2I − P) > 0 and v(2I − M) > 0. Thus diagonal entries of P and M lie in {0, 1}.

The combined directed support is strongly connected: otherwise the reciprocal matrix A₊⁻¹A₋ would be block diagonal, contradicting the lowest nonzero coefficient between different blocks and disjoint support. Every edge therefore lies on a simple cycle of length ℓ ≤ 3. The inequalities wᵢⱼvᵢ < 2vⱼ, with wᵢⱼ = max(Pᵢⱼ, Mᵢⱼ), give a product of positive integer edge weights less than 2ℓ. Each off-diagonal coefficient sum is at most 7.

steps.title: 2. Enumerate constants and solve all lifts
steps.html:
The finite enumeration retains 180 canonical constant pairs after positivity, constant symplecticity and indecomposability checks. Introduce one exponent variable for every unit of coefficient mass, allowing equal exponents within one sign. The Laurent identity becomes equality of two finite multisets of integer linear forms.

The feasibility problem includes strict row support and disjointness of opposite signs. It has no delay cutoff. Exactly 164 constant pairs have no lift and 16 survive. The saved UNSAT formulas cover the 164 exclusions and the 16 family-coverage checks.

steps.title: 3. Identify every admissible lift
steps.html:
For each survivor, matching equal Laurent exponents produces a homogeneous rational linear subspace. Reduction modulo its row-reduced equations verifies the polynomial identity symbolically. The subspace has dimension three and is generated by the representative exponent vector and two relative species shifts.

An unbounded solver query asks for an admissible lift outside this subspace. Its UNSAT result establishes coverage at every delay. In the Admissible lifts view, the exact test is r′ᵢ = λrᵢ ∈ ℤ>0 and p′ = λp + sᵢ − sⱼ ∈ ℤ with 0 < p′ < r′ᵢ, where s₃ = 0.

steps.title: 4. Certify periodicity and distinguish classes
steps.html:
The reconstructed exchange matrix returns after each time step and its relabelling. Integer mutation of the principal C-matrix reaches a negative permutation matrix in both time directions. The cited two-sided reddening criterion proves finite type. The recorded labelled period is the first positive return of that C-matrix in the displayed time coordinate.

Integral dilation separates time into residue classes; integral species shifts reindex solutions. Clearing denominators extends preservation of finite type to all admissible rational parameters. The 16 constant pairs distinguish the families, and canonical connected-slice encodings distinguish their slice classes. Consequently simultaneous positivity is also sufficient in this scope.

4.decomposable: Decomposable rank-four data are direct sums with rank partitions 3 + 1, 2 + 2, 2 + 1 + 1 or 1 + 1 + 1 + 1, using the corresponding lower-rank classifications. Component time scales can be chosen independently.

steps.title: 1. Reduce to bounded constant matrices
steps.html:
Let P = N₊(1) and M = N₋(1). Simultaneous positivity supplies a common v > 0 with v(2I − P) > 0 and v(2I − M) > 0. Diagonal entries are 0 or 1 and all principal minors of 2I − P and 2I − M are positive.

Indecomposability and the reciprocal identity for A₊⁻¹A₋ force the combined directed support to be strongly connected. Every arrow lies on a simple cycle of length ℓ ≤ 4. Multiplying max(Pᵢⱼ, Mᵢⱼ)vᵢ < 2vⱼ around this cycle bounds each off-diagonal coefficient sum by 2ℓ − 1 ≤ 15. This bound is independent of the delays.

steps.title: 2. Enumerate 4,865 constants and apply parity
steps.kind: Exact enumeration and an elementary obstruction
steps.html:
Relabel so that v₁ ≥ v₂ ≥ v₃ ≥ v₄. In column j, the sum of entries above the diagonal is at most 1 − Cⱼⱼ for C = P or M. There are 120 choices of the diagonal and upper triangle per matrix. The enumerator fills lower entries using integer bounds and solves the constant symplectic equations with an invertible leading principal block.

Exact connectivity, positivity and canonical-form checks leave 4,865 pairs. Independently verified positive vectors certify the retained inequalities. The rank-three specialization reproduces the full set of 180 earlier constants.

The diagonal Laurent polynomial (A₊A₋*)ᵢᵢ is reciprocal and has constant coefficient 2, where F*(z) = F(z−1)T. Its value at 1 must therefore be even. This excludes 4,405 pairs and leaves 460.

steps.title: 3. Exclude the chain pattern
steps.html:
Three constant IDs have the chain pattern treated in §3 of the manuscript; one is already excluded by parity. The two further exclusions leave 458 pairs.

The top chain equations force equal delays R on its first three species. With q = zR, F = 1 + q and the nonnegative Laurent polynomials X, Y, Z, W, H defined in that section (H ≠ 0), the remaining equations are:

Y = FX + H,   FY = qX + Z,   F(Z − W) = qY.
Z = (1 + q + q²)X + FH.

Thus Y and Z have the same lowest exponent d. Since R > 0, qY starts at d + R. The last equation forces W to share the nonzero coefficient of Z at d. The opposite signs in entry (4, 3) then have a common exponent, contradicting disjoint support. The complete definitions and pattern matrices are in the linked manuscript.

steps.title: 4. Solve all lifts without a delay cutoff
steps.html:
Of the remaining 458 constant pairs, 421 have no polynomial lift and 37 survive. Each coefficient unit gets its own exponent variable, so coincident monomials and coefficients greater than one are included. Equality of Laurent polynomials is encoded by equality of multiplicities of linear exponent forms, or by exact sorting networks.

Each surviving lift space has dimension four and is exactly the span of its representative and the three relative species shifts. Symbolic reduction verifies the identity on that space; an UNSAT query excludes every admissible lift outside it. Integer variables are unbounded. For the homogeneous real-arithmetic check, rational density within each rational linear branch and clearing denominators justify equivalence to integer feasibility.

All 4,865 saved queries replay to UNSAT: 4,407 elementary exclusions justified by the parity and chain lemmas, 421 remaining no-lift checks and 37 coverage checks. The elementary formulas alone do not replace those lemmas.

steps.title: 5. Prove sufficiency and check distinctness
steps.html:
For each representative, reconstruct the exchange matrix on the vertices (i, p), 0 ≤ p < rᵢ. Mutate at (i, 0) for all species and apply (i, p) ↦ (i, p − 1 mod rᵢ). The exact verifier checks exchange-matrix return, commuting simultaneous mutations and inverse-step consistency. Two-sided negative permutation C-matrices certify finite type via the cited criterion.

Species shifts and time dilation preserve finite type; clearing denominators handles the rational case. The constants distinguish the 37 families. Canonical connected-slice encodings exhaust cyclic rotations, adjacent commuting mutations and sign exchange, and their full encodings are all distinct.

An independent degree-two enumeration considers all 310 = 59,049 symmetric signed matrices. Its nine classes are 1, 2, 3, 28, 29, 30, 31, 34 and 35. Use the “All delays = 2” filter to inspect them.

1.statement: The scalar positivity bound, reciprocal parity identity and extremal exponents give exactly two admissible rescaling families, modulo sign exchange. Their representative periods are 2 and 5.

2.statement: The six representatives reproduce Table 1 in its original order and sign convention. Theorem 1.5 proves completeness under change of slices; Lemmas 3.6–3.9 describe the polynomial lift families. Exact mutation certificates were recomputed locally.

5.decomposable: Decomposable data are direct sums of indecomposable components, with independent scales and sign choices.

steps.title: 1. Reduce to a finite constant search
steps.html: The ordered positive-vector argument bounds off-diagonal coefficient sums by 31. Each sign has 6! = 720 upper-triangular possibilities. Exact row solving, ordered path bounds, principal minors, parity and the simultaneous-positive cone leave exactly 4,697 pairs. The same enumerator reproduces all 460 earlier rank-four candidates.

steps.title: 2. Classify every polynomial lift
steps.html:
All 4,642 excluded pairs have no admissible polynomial lift. Necessary relations include principal subdata, the monomial-tree attachment lemma and an alternating-chain identity. In the last case, constant ID 2067, the latter forces a chain of 17 alternating terms. Rational and integer linear-arithmetic encodings are equivalent after homogeneous normalization and clearing denominators.

The 55 survivors each have one five-dimensional matching space, generated by the representative and four species shifts. Every outside-space query is UNSAT. All 4,697 exclusion or coverage queries were replayed successfully.

steps.title: 3. Certify finite type and distinctness
steps.kind: Exact principal-coefficient mutation and slice loops
steps.html:
Both mutation directions reach negative permutation C-matrices, and each representative has an exact labelled return. These certify finite type by the cited periodicity criterion.

Terminal permutation cycle lengths distinguish 42 singleton groups. The remaining 13 representatives form five groups; exhaustive cyclic rotations, commuting mutations and both signs give distinct full minima inside every group. This proves catalogue distinctness without claiming a global canonical form for the singleton groups.

steps.title: 4. Identify families, quivers and exponents
steps.html: The notes compare exact polynomials with every RSG and SG parameter list of rank five, and ADE/tadpole tensor constructors. Every quiver identification has a replayable integer mutation path. The thesis determinant formula gives interval-certified root multiplicities, independently verified from the logarithmic mutation Jacobian. These identifications and spectra enrich the classification; they do not supply its completeness argument.

6.decomposable: Decomposable data are direct sums of indecomposable components, with independent scales and sign choices.

steps.title: 1. Exhaust the necessary constant data
steps.kind: Exact finite enumeration with hereditary pruning
steps.html:
Simultaneous positivity bounds each off-diagonal coefficient sum by 63. Ordering a positive vector leaves 7! = 5,040 upper-triangular choices per sign. Every unordered pair of these choices is processed. Exact row solving, column and path bounds, parity, principal minors and the positive cone test are combined with the completed lower-rank classification on eligible principal blocks.

All 5,040 upper tasks are complete. They retain 32,087 candidate pairs, including the earlier unpruned checkpoints. This is a complete search after necessary exclusions; the number does not count the unpruned constant set. The stronger column bounds reproduce exactly all 460 rank-four and 4,697 rank-five reference candidates.

steps.title: 2. Settle every polynomial lift
steps.kind: Unbounded exponents and a proved finite pulse reduction
steps.html:
Exactly 31,979 constant pairs have no admissible polynomial lift. The other 108 each have one six-dimensional matching space, generated by its representative and five species shifts. Every outside-space query is UNSAT.

The final difficult exclusions use a single monomial attachment to a classified core. After normalizing the core, the new row is a deterministic integer recurrence forced by two or three pulses. If h is the largest core delay and S is the prescribed off-diagonal row mass, the relative new delay is at most (S + 1)h. The common rational time scale remains unrestricted.

All 32,087 exclusion or coverage checks have been replayed. The 45 pulse exclusions were also checked by a separate C++ program exhaustively testing 2,887,440 pulse positions. Read the finite-bound proof and its verification.

steps.title: 3. Certify periodicity and distinctness
steps.kind: Exact mutations and complete slice comparisons
steps.html:
Each representative has two-sided reddening certificates and an exact labelled return. These supply the finite-type certificate for every admissible scale and shift in its complete family.

Terminal permutation cycle lengths distinguish 78 representatives immediately. The remaining 30 form nine groups. Exhaustive cyclic rotations, commuting mutations, relabeling and both signs give distinct canonical minima within every group. The largest combined orbit has 46,080 states. The C++ comparison engine agrees with the independent Python results on all 16 saved control cases.

steps.title: 4. Record families, quivers, matrices and exponents
steps.kind: Exact certificates attached to each entry
steps.html:
The notes identify all 64 RSG and 8 SG parameter lists of rank six, 10 ADE/tadpole Zamolodchikov matches, and 16 commuting Cartan constructions; these categories overlap. Twenty-three entries have no identification among the checked constructors.

All 108 connected slice quivers have exact class certificates: 74 Dynkin, 27 mutation-infinite, two exceptional, and five from punctured spheres. The last surface certificate reconstructs and checks an eight-punctured sphere directly.

Each entry gives A₊(1), A₋(1), both inverse matrix products, and the multiplicities from Mizuno’s determinant formula. An independent interval calculation of the mutation Jacobian verifies all 108 spectra. The unit-circle plot and its table retain every multiplicity.
